Every script is in the measurement because every script runs in one of these workflows; the step runner is a root module because it is the machinery the workflow's own tests execute rather than something a workflow runs. The floor is the LOWER of the two cells that will read this tree, not this box's number: the ubuntu-latest/3.13 cell has measured three lines differently on impact_loc.py (70 missed there against 67 here), which moves this 4017-statement ratio by 0.07 points, so this box reads 81.8 and the runner reads 81.7. Pinning the floor to 81.7 rather than 81.8 is what lets the first push to main pass — a floor above the runner's own reading is a red nothing in this repository can lower — and that first raise then re-pins the floor to whatever the runner actually measures, which is the only figure here that was ever a real measurement of the cell the ratchet is calibrated to. That runner figure is therefore derived from one observed 3-line difference, not measured; if the runner's difference is larger on a given run the first push is red, loudly, and a human re-derives it. Re-derive the floor, never carry it: the denominator moves whenever a renderer does, and a floor carried across a rebase measures a tree that no longer exists. The fourteenth file, scripts/ci/counter.py, arrived with the change that made the former speed workflow judge a load-invariant counter instead of a wall-clock duration, and the record moved 13 to 14 here rather than silently comparing a fourteen-file measurement against a thirteen-file floor; `raise` refuses outright when the measured file count differs from the `files` recorded here, because a percentage cannot announce that its own denominator changed. A same-population coverage change moves the number silently, and only a person re-deriving it catches that, which is why this file has been re-derived rather than carried at every step: 73.1 when the baseline gained a per-population sub-document, 73.0 when the syscall instrument was dropped for costing 12.8x the work it measured (the denominator shrank by 58 and the miss count by 10, so the ratio moved a tenth of a point UP on a change that deleted code — the same-direction surprise, in the other direction, and recorded rather than absorbed), then 80.0 on the rebase onto main, 81.3 after the module split took the population from fifteen files to eighteen, and 81.6 when the committed counter baseline landed without adding a shipped module.
